tagline: Down the Alsea from the Coast Range's top to the sea.
intro: The byway starts near I-5 at Tangent, named for a run of railroad with no curves for more than 20 miles, and goes through Corvallis and Philomath before turning southwest onto OR 34. From there it follows the Alsea River on an often narrow, twisting road through Alsea and Tidewater, near the head of the tide, to Waldport and US 101.
Two spurs climb away from it. One goes up Marys Peak Road, built by the Civilian Conservation Corps, and the other runs ten miles down South Fork Road to Alsea Falls.
season: Travel Oregon lists it as a year-round drive.

moments.title: Marys Peak
moments.text: From the top of the Coast Range, 4,097 feet, the view runs east over the Willamette Valley to the Cascades and, on a clear day, west to the Pacific.

moments.title: Alsea Falls
moments.text: The falls come down 30 feet in stair steps among old-growth Douglas fir and western redcedar, with a campground and trails alongside.

moments.title: Waldport
moments.text: Many early settlers were German, so the town became wald, forest, plus port, and here the Alsea River slows and widens into Alsea Bay.

practical: Marys Peak Road stays open in winter but is not maintained then, and a high-clearance four-wheel-drive vehicle or chains on all four wheels are required.

sources.label: Travel Oregon, Marys Peak to Pacific Scenic Byway
